analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows an automated cloud migration factory pattern designed by Versant to migrate on-premises servers to AWS target accounts in ~10 minutes. First, agents on the on-premises servers push TCP connection and performance metadata to AWS Application Discovery Service, while CloudEndure handles continuous block-by-block replication to an EC2 Hot Replica in AWS. The migration team populates target configurations (tags, IP addresses, subnets, target accounts) into DynamoDB. When ready, the migration team triggers the migration command via Slack, which invokes the Migration Factory EC2 instance via API. The Migration Factory queries DynamoDB for target specifications and Application Discovery Service for network/sizing details, then signals CloudEndure via API to stop replication. Finally, the Migration Factory creates/shares the AMI and launches the properly sized and tagged EC2 Target instance in the target AWS account.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows how OLX Autos built an internal developer platform (Orion portal) on AWS to rapidly provision multi-service environments at lower cost using 100% EC2 Spot instances. A developer accesses the Orion portal via HTTPS. Route 53 performs DNS resolution pointing to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB routes incoming requests to Kubernetes pods managed by Amazon EKS running on EC2 Spot instances. To handle microservice job creation and potential Spot instance terminations, when EKS triggers jobs for microservices, it sends an event to Amazon SNS. SNS fans out the event message to an Amazon SQS queue. If a Spot instance terminates mid-job, the replacement job on a new Spot instance watches SQS to retrieve state and resume unfinished tasks cleanly.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The diagram presents CloudHealth SecureState's real-time security monitoring architecture on AWS. analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Marathon Oil's automated drone imagery processing pipeline. Drones upload flight images to a third-party software. A CloudWatch Event triggers AWS Step Functions on a scheduled basis, which orchestrates Lambda functions to query the third-party software via API, copy image files into AWS S3, and store raster proxies in an on-premises database. On-premises mapping software accesses image files directly from S3 using AWS Storage Gateway.
